idiom_name: generator pipeline / itertools with an explicit terminal, or a hand-written transducer over functools.reduce
implementation_notes: Python's idiomatic answer is lazy composition rather than reducing-function transformers: generator functions/expressions and itertools (islice, takewhile, batched, groupby, chain) compose over any iterable in one pass without intermediate collections, and the terminal is an explicit consumer - a for loop, sum, list(), max(). functools.reduce exposes exactly the reducing function a transducer must wrap, so the faithful form is a ~15-line hand-written module (a Transducer is a callable taking a reducer and returning a reducer, composed with a small transducers(*stages) helper); third-party ports exist (the transducer package on PyPI, cognitect-labs/transducers-python) but are not de-facto standard. What replaces the classic structure: generator pipelines replace the classic structure for iterator-to-iterator work; the transducer form is still justified when one stack must also drive non-iterable sinks (coroutines, push events, executors) or when early termination and a completion/flush step must be part of the transformation value.
code_sketch:
import functools
def transducers(*stages):                    # a transducer stack: rf -> rf
    return lambda rf: functools.reduce(lambda r, st: st(r), stages, rf)
def mapping(f):   return lambda rf: lambda acc, x: rf(acc, f(x))
def filtering(p): return lambda rf: lambda acc, x: rf(acc, x) if p(x) else acc

xf = transducers(mapping(square), filtering(is_even))   # reusable transformation value
total = functools.reduce(xf(lambda acc, x: acc + x), range(1_000_000), 0)
# idiomatic equivalent, no transducer: sum(x * x for x in range(1_000_000) if x % 2 == 0)
pitfalls: Generators are single-use: a consumed pipeline yields nothing on a second pass, so composable pipelines must be factories (def pipeline(src): ...) rather than module-level generator objects.

Generator pipelines cannot express completion or early termination: buffering stages must be rebuilt with itertools (batched, groupby) and take becomes itertools.islice, otherwise the whole source is consumed.
functools.reduce without an initializer returns the first element for a one-element input and raises for an empty one - the wrong accumulator seed for a transducer application.
Per-element Python frames make a hand-written transducer chain slower than a fused loop for small or hot data.
